title: Transfer Learning and Fine-Tuning
overview: Reusing a network pretrained on a large dataset gives strong features with little labeled data. You can freeze the backbone or fine-tune it with a small learning rate.
objectives: Choose between feature extraction and fine-tuning
Replace and train a new classification head
Set learning rates for pretrained versus new layers

method.title: Pretrained features
method.body: Early layers learn general features that transfer across tasks.

method.title: Feature extraction
method.body: Freeze the backbone and train only a new head; best for tiny datasets.

method.title: Fine-tuning
method.body: Unfreeze some or all layers and train with a small learning rate, often smaller for the backbone than the head.

method.title: Domain gap
method.body: The further the target data is from pretraining data, the more layers you should adapt.

pseudocode:
model = load_pretrained()
for p in model.backbone.parameters(): p.requires_grad = False
model.head = Linear(feat_dim, num_classes)
train(model.head)
# optional: unfreeze backbone, lr = 1e-5

playground.starterCode:
import torch, torch.nn as nn
backbone = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(16, 32), nn.ReLU())  # stands in for a pretrained model
head = nn.Linear(32, 3)
for p in backbone.parameters():
    p.requires_grad = False
params = [p for p in list(backbone.parameters()) + list(head.parameters()) if p.requires_grad]
print("trainable parameters:", sum(p.numel() for p in params))
print("frozen parameters:", sum(p.numel() for p in backbone.parameters()))

quiz.question: With a very small target dataset, a safe first approach is:
options: Freeze the backbone and train a new head

quiz.question: Why use a smaller learning rate for pretrained layers?
options: To avoid destroying useful learned features
